overview: Two immunoglobulin classes with very specialised roles — mucosal defence versus allergic and anti-parasite response.
genZNote: IgA: the security guard stationed at every mucosal doorway. IgE: the hair-trigger alarm behind allergic reactions.

aspects.label: Main Role
aspects.valueA: Provides mucosal immunity — found in saliva, tears, breast milk, and respiratory/gut secretions.
aspects.valueB: Mediates allergic reactions and defence against parasitic worms (helminths).

aspects.label: Relative Abundance
aspects.valueA: Second most abundant antibody class, especially concentrated at mucosal surfaces.
aspects.valueB: Least abundant antibody class in normal circulation.

aspects.label: Clinical Relevance
aspects.valueA: Deficiency linked to recurrent respiratory/gut infections.
aspects.valueB: Elevated levels linked to allergies, asthma, and parasitic infections.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Breast milk is especially rich in IgA, giving newborns passive mucosal immunity through breastfeeding.
overlay.memoryTrick: IgA = mucosAl surfaces. IgE = allErgy and parasites.
overlay.commonMisconception: IgE is not the most abundant antibody just because it's the most clinically talked-about in allergies — it's actually present in the smallest quantities of all antibody classes.
